scenes.title: The plan

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: First, Volatility (sigma): annualised standard deviation of returns. Daily sigma about annual sigma divided by the square root of 365 (crypto trades every day). Next, Value at risk (value at risk): a loss level you'd expect to exceed only rarely (for example 1 day in 20 at 95%). Parametric 1-day value at risk about 1.65 times daily sigma times position. It assumes normal returns; crypto has fat tails, so real losses exceed value at risk more often. Use it as a floor, plus stress tests (11.4). Then, Max drawdown: the largest peak-to-trough fall. Ask: could I live through it, and would my policies survive it? Also, Correlation: in crashes, correlations between crypto assets rise towards 1. Diversifying within crypto helps less when you need it most. And finally, Sizing: volatility targeting (size so each position contributes similar risk); the Kelly criterion gives a theoretical maximum bet size from edge and odds, but estimates are noisy, so professionals use a small fraction of it or skip it.
scenes.cap: First, Volatility (σ): annualised standard deviation of returns. Daily σ ≈ annual σ ÷ √365 (crypto trades every day). scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. $100,000 of ETH at 70% annual volatility: the calculator gives daily sigma about 3.66%, 1-day 95% value at risk about $6,046. Real single-day falls have been far larger (in March 2020, ETH fell by roughly 40% in a day). So: value at risk for day-to-day sizing, stress tests for survival.

scenes.q: What happens to correlations in a crash?
scenes.vo: Question three. What happens to correlations in a crash? [[pause 4]] The answer: They tend to rise towards 1.
